appearance_facts.fact: The May bar is a dark red rectangle whose top edge sits just above the 10,000 gridline, making it the shortest bar on the chart.

appearance_facts.location: Jan bar, second position from the left
appearance_facts.fact: The Jan bar is the tallest bar, with its top edge aligned exactly with the 40,000 gridline.
The Apr bar top edge is just below the 30,000 gridline.
The Jun bar top edge is between the 15,000 and 20,000 gridlines, closer to 17,500.
The Feb bar top edge aligns with the 20,000 gridline.
The Mar bar top edge is between the 25,000 and 30,000 gridlines, closer to 27,000.
All bars share the same dark red fill color; there is no legend or second series.
The vertical axis is labeled 'Release volume (m3)' with a break mark near the origin and tick labels from 10,000 to 40,000 in 5,000 increments.

No numerical annotation is printed; top aligns with the 40,000 tick.

public_definitions: User goal: 'Review the monthly reservoir release dashboard and decide whether May should be handled as a standard low-release case or escalated as a critical low-release anomaly for this reporting cycle.'
Option 1: 'Route May to standard low-release follow-up'.
Option 2: 'Escalate May to critical low-release anomaly review'.
Option 3: 'Send May to background monthly record filing'.
uncertain: The exact numeric value of the May bar is not printed; it is visually just above the 10,000 m3 tick (roughly 8,000–9,000 m3 above the broken origin baseline, i.e., a very low release), but the precise figure cannot be read.

No explicit threshold or policy table is provided on the page that defines the boundary between 'standard low-release' and 'critical low-release anomaly', so the escalation decision must be inferred from the chart's relative magnitudes.
The X-axis month order (Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, Mar, May) is non-chronological; it is read literally as displayed and no time-series trend is implied.
The Y-axis break mark near the origin means the baseline is not zero; the absolute low value of May relative to a true zero cannot be confirmed from the chart alone.
